$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the first column of the matrix $P?$

activity_context.topic_title: Jordan Canonical Decomposition of a 2x2 Matrix

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-16 & -25 \\ 9 & 14\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the first column of the matrix $P?$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,z=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that the Jordan matrix $J$ consists of one Jordan block $J={J}_{2}(-1).$ 

Therefore, the columns of $P$ form the following chain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{2}(-1) & : & {v}_{2}\overset{A-(-1)I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-(-1)I\,}{\to }0 & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the first column of $P$ is an eigenvector corresponding to $\lambda =-1.$ 

Now, computing $A-(-1)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}-16 & -25 \\ 9 & 14\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-15 & -25 \\ 9 & 15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Among the given vectors, only $z$ is an eigenvector of $A,$ since

$$
(A-(-1)I)z=[\begin{aligned}-15 & -25 \\ 9 & 15\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

and we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\overset{A-(-1)I\,}{\to }0.\end{aligned}
$$

The other vectors do not satisfy this condition.
